message:
Hi Elias,
I am looking for an expert in financial modeling to assist us with our project in Tasmania, Australia. Let me know if you can help.
You can count on my help, Maren. I’m available.

Hi Mari,
I hope you're doing well.

Just wanted to check in and let you know that if you have any requirements related to financial modeling, business valuation, budgeting, forecasting, or accounting and finance, I'd be happy to help.

Please feel free to reach out whenever you need support. I look forward to the opportunity to work with you.

Regards,
Elias Mercer

Since we already have the financial-model template and the data, we need someone to check that data and refine the model. Hello Elias—could you confirm whether you can do this and tell me how much you would charge?

Before we begin, Maren, here is how I would approach the review. I’m happy to help, and my model-review rate is $35/hour rather than a flat fee.

A financial model cannot reliably be reviewed by spot-checking a single section, because one incorrect input or formula can flow through the entire model and affect its outputs. A proper review therefore requires working through it end to end and correcting or tightening anything that needs attention.

For your model, I would compare the entered data with the source documents, verify that formulas and cross-sheet links operate correctly, and assess whether the key assumptions are reasonable and adequately supported. I would also examine the valuation work—including WACC, cost of equity, Beta, and how each has been applied—as well as the tax treatment, since small mistakes in those areas can remain unnoticed until they alter the output.

After you share the template and data, I can review them briefly and estimate the likely number of hours. That will give you a clear indication of the expected cost before work starts.

If this arrangement works for you, please send the files whenever they are ready.

Best,
Elias Mercer

Attached are the Excel template and additional project information for your review, Elias. We are currently preparing a financial model for government submission in connection with a potential PPP project.

For the project to be viable and bankable, a key requirement is that the model clearly demonstrate and justify the need for availability-style payments. Please confirm whether you can support us in developing it. There may be errors that need checking, and we also need the finished model to look professional, clear, and strongly presented.
Are you available?
A confirmation will follow shortly; I’m currently reviewing the files you supplied.
Okay—until your confirmation comes through, I’ll remain on standby.
I am unable to download the file "Integrated\_finance\_Scenario\_V7." If possible, could you share it as a PDF instead?
Because the pdf version contains many formatting errors, I do not recommend using it. Please open the file with excel instead.

During the download, an error appears that identifies the file as unsafe and blocks access. It says that anyone who really wants to access it must contact Customer Support, and its online-safety guidance directs users to the Upwork Security Center.
The warning being shown to you—is it that exact one?
Why you’re receiving that safety warning remains unclear to me; I downloaded the file successfully without encountering the problem.

After reviewing the other 2 files, I found that the Excel template you provided is a generic single-highway toll-road PPP model—specifically, a standard PPIAF/Operis educational template. It cannot accommodate the required cargonests structure of 12 sites, the separate revenue streams for parking, pods, fleet subscriptions, the digital platform, and EV charging, or the availability-payment comparison between Case F and Case G.

This is therefore not a matter of fixing a few errors. The model needs to be substantially rebuilt while retaining the template’s financial engine, including its debt schedule and 3-statement structure. Its revenue, capex, and payment modules must be replaced so they reflect your requirements.

My understanding is that the scope would include, but not be limited to:
- Building capex and opex site by site across gateway, regional, and corridor-support typologies
- Modeling all revenue streams separately: parking, pods, fleet contracts, digital, and ancillary
- Developing the capital stack and debt schedule, with DSCR/IRR outputs
- Sizing the availability payment endogenously against a target DSCR of 1.55-1.75x
- Comparing Case F, which is user-funded, with Case G, the PPP structure that includes an availability payment
- Running sensitivities for traffic, occupancy, capex, interest rates, and opex
- Applying clean, presentation-ready formatting suitable for government submission

Before the build starts, I will need the CargoNest feasibility and demand study referenced as Transitgrid-Market-Forecast. I will also need confirmed point estimates for the key inputs because the brief currently provides ranges. Those can be agreed base-case figures, or you can authorize me to select the range midpoints.

The estimated effort is 65-90 hours over approximately 9-12 days, depending on how quickly the inputs are confirmed.

Billing would be at $35/hour against milestones covering the structure build, revenue and payment logic, scenario sensitivities, final formatting, and Dashboards. This will allow you to monitor both progress and cost as the work proceeds.

If useful, we can begin with a quick call to confirm the scope.

Best,
Elias Mercer
The total cost cannot exceed my $900 budget. Could we therefore replace hourly billing with a fixed-price contract?

To build the model efficiently, I first need confirmation of the deadline and the availability of the following information:

1\. The CargoNest feasibility/demand study referenced in the brief as Transitgrid-Market-Forecast
2\. Confirmed capex point figures for each site typology—gateway, regional, and corridor-support—or permission to use the midpoint of the ranges in the brief
3\. Any updated or firm figures for land values or lease costs, opex, tariffs such as parking and pod rates, and fleet subscription pricing
4\. Confirmed financing terms, if lender or investor indications exist, including the interest rate, tenor, and equity percentage; otherwise, I will use the ranges provided
5\. Any available site-level information, including traffic counts and whether land is leased or owned
6\. Your preferred currency and price base year; I am assuming AUD with a 2031 base, so please confirm

If any item is not yet available, let me know and I will use the assumptions stated in the brief while flagging them clearly in the model. Providing the available material together will reduce back-and-forth delays, let me move directly into the build, and help manage the project budget.

Thanks

Because we want to move as quickly as possible, could we target late TUESDAY for delivery? Please begin the model build using the information currently available, and we can refine it as further inputs are confirmed.

The present data position is as follows:

1) The attached CargoNest feasibility/demand analysis, TransitGrid-Market-Forecast, may be used directionally together with the assumptions in the brief.

2) Capex figures have not yet been finalized. The overall program is presently estimated at 225–270M, so please use the midpoint of the ranges in the brief. The attached business case also shows the midpoint set.

3) Firm figures for land values, lease costs, opex, and pricing are not yet available. Use the indicative ranges in the document and clearly flag every resulting assumption.

4) Financing terms remain unconfirmed, with no lender or investor commitments at this stage. Please apply standard market assumptions selected from the ranges provided.

5) Structured site-level information, including traffic counts and land status, is not yet available. We only have a general traffic count for each corridor, so the missing site-level details must be modeled.

6) Use AUD and a 2031 base year for the model.

7) The core requirement is to model correctly and clearly demonstrate why availability-style payments are necessary to make the project viable and bankable. This is the primary information the government wants to see.

Accordingly, treat the brief and attached materials as the main reference points, annotate all assumptions clearly, and proceed now. We will iterate when more definitive inputs become available. Please let me know if anything critical arises during the build.

Before I can begin the work, the contract must be awarded. Thank you for providing the information; please award it so I can start.

Regards
Because the government will review the model, please ensure the modeling is flawless and the work is completed to a high standard.
Thanks for the offer; I accept and will do my best on the work.

Please confirm the following six items:

1. Site list conflict
The Demand Analysis report and the Business Case present two different 12-site networks. The Demand Analysis includes Cedarwick-Halston, Fairhaven-Rosmere, Alderby, and Kestrel Bay, whereas the Business Case includes Copper Glen, Ravensfield-Aurora Plant, and Juniper Wells instead. Since the Business Case provides the capital allocation figures, should its site list be treated as final for the financial model?

2. Opex figure conflict
For the 12-site network, the original brief gives steady-state operating costs of CAD 48-64M/year, while Appendix 1 of the Business Case reports annual O&M of only CAD 4.2-5.6M/year. That is a roughly 11x difference. Which figure, or underlying cost basis, should drive the financial model's operating-cost assumption?

3. Availability payment sizing target
Should the availability payment be calculated only to meet the target minimum DSCR of 1.65x, or must it also achieve a minimum equity IRR within the 16-24% infrastructure-equity target range cited by the Business Case? Although the current DSCR-only approach reaches the coverage target, equity IRR remains negative even after the availability payment is added.

4. Programwide/shared costs
In addition to $201.5M of site-level capex, the Business Case's $234M Reference Case contains $18.4M for shared programwide costs, including the digital platform and program management, plus a $14M reserve/13th-site allowance. Should the model show these as separate line items, or should they remain outside the scope of the 12-site financial model?

5. Financing terms confirmation
Senior debt in the Business Case covers 45-60% of capital, is priced at 425-575bps above Government of Canada bond yields, and may be supplemented by optional mezzanine debt. Our current model instead uses a simplified 55/45 debt/equity split with a flat 9% rate. At this stage, is that single-tranche structure acceptable, or should mezzanine financing be modeled separately?

6. Tax/depreciation
At present, the model applies a flat 34% tax to EBITDA and includes no depreciation shield. Is that sufficient for this stage, or should depreciation/CCA (Capital Cost Allowance) be incorporated because this will be an actual government submission?

The six points should be handled as follows:

1\. Site list
For the model, treat the Business Case site list as final.

2\. Opex figures
The correct program-level operating assumption is the original brief's CAD 48–64M/year range. Because the Appendix amount appears incomplete or understated, it must not be used for the full-network model.

3\. Availability payment approach
Size the availability payment to meet both of these targets:

- A minimum DSCR of ~1.65x; and

- A minimum equity IRR in the 16–20% range.

If relying on DSCR alone produces negative equity returns, the model must not use that approach.

4\. Program-wide/shared costs
Digital-platform, program-management, and contingency/reserve costs should appear as separate line items within total program capex rather than being excluded.

5\. Financing structure
For this stage, retain the streamlined 55/45 debt/equity structure at ~9%. There is no need to add a separate mezzanine layer yet; we can refine the financing after engaging lenders.

6\. Tax/depreciation
Instead of the flat tax treatment, model CCA/depreciation properly using the applicable standard Canadian Capital Cost Allowance classes for each asset type—for example, Class 6 for buildings, Class 50 for clean energy equipment, and Class 12 for furniture/fixtures. Proper treatment is essential to a credible government submission because it will materially affect both the tax shield and equity returns.

The immediate priority is to produce a coherent base-case model quickly and then iterate on it.

Although the model is being finalized, its figures remain projections. At this stage, the main objective is to give the government sufficiently robust financial evidence that an availability-style payment is necessary. The model must clearly show that user fees alone cannot make the project viable or bankable.
To ensure the final numbers make sense and appear credible, please review the model thoroughly. You may make any changes that would improve it.
Sure noted
Could you let me know what progress has been made? I haven't received a recent update from you.
Hi. Hopefully, I will be able to share the 1st draft next Monday.
Since I am unable to download the file here, could you send it through gmail to elias.mercer@cedarbridge.example? Thanks.
The requested file has just been sent by email. It looks as though you may not have started working on the model, so I need this work to be prioritized.
The work is already 55% complete.
For your review, I will share the draft Next Monday.
I need a version that I can understand, because the presentation is unclear and I cannot follow the figures or see how they were generated.
For the model, we have to find a simpler approach.
A short version is what I will prepare and share, no problem.

Reviewing and following the current model is difficult because it is too complex. Its dashboards also fail to show decision-makers the essential information clearly, including project returns, debt performance, and overall bankability. Rather than communicating the investment story, the model places too much emphasis on calculations.

The revised model should therefore be simpler, easier to understand, and easier to audit, with stronger dashboards and project-finance analysis. My goal is a model that works technically while also making a clear case that the project is financially viable, bankable, and attractive to investors.
In addition to the main working model, I will prepare a short presentation file. That will not be an issue.
So that anyone seeking more detail can consult the main working model, the presentation file will include references to it.
Attached for your review is the Excel working file. If any figure raises questions or requires clarification, please let me know.

Hi Mari,

Sure I will make the required changes. The model looks detailed because it's built on individual drivers each revenue stream (parking, pods, fleet, digital, ancillary) and each cost line is calculated separately from its own assumption, rather than typed in as one lump number. I did it this way on purpose so that when the government reviewer asks "where does this figure come from?", every number traces back to a source on the Assumptions tab. That's what makes it defensible.

The trade-off is exactly what you're feeling , more drivers , more rows to look at. I can go either way, so I'd rather you decide:

(a) Keep it driver-based (defensible, more rows), or
(b) Collapse it to a summary model a handful of top-level lines (total revenue, total cost, debt, availability payment, returns) with the detailed build moved to hidden/backing tabs. The front page becomes very short and clean; the detail is still there if anyone wants to open it.

I can make it a one-pager but still has the audit trail underneath. Tell me which you'd prefer and I'll restructure accordingly.

A few structuring options came up that could genuinely strengthen your pitch to government. These aren't in the model yet; I'm flagging them because any one of them could be the thing that makes the submission stand out. Such as:

1\. Government-funds-first, then sublet against the income ("build-then-transfer"). The Province funds or co-funds the capex up front (cheapest capital in the room), then leases/sublets the operating network to a private operator who pays a concession fee back against parking, pod and fleet income. This flips the story instead of government paying an availability payment out, government recovers a return in. I can model this as a third case (Case H) it may show a far lower net cost to the Province than the availability-payment route.

2\. Availability payment now, tapering to a revenue-share later. Rather than a flat 24-year payment, structure it so the Province pays more in the early ramp-up years (when revenue is thin) and then, once the network matures and throws off surplus cash, the Province shares in the upside clawing back part of what it paid in. Same bankability, lower lifetime net cost, and it reads as a partnership rather than a subsidy.

3\. Toll / user-levy overlay on the corridor. If these sites sit on designated freight corridors, a small per-truck corridor levy (or a portion of an existing road-use charge) could be ring-fenced to part-fund the network. That directly reduces the availability payment the government has to find from general revenue the users who benefit help pay.

4\. Phased equity exit / refinancing at stabilisation. Model the Province (or the original equity) selling down its stake to a pension fund or infrastructure fund once the network is built and de-risked (around year 9-12). De-risked, cash-yielding infrastructure sells at a premium so early capital gets recycled out at a profit and redeployed into Phase 4, instead of being locked up for 24 years.

5\. Anchor / cornerstone tenant revenue. Lock in four or five large fleets or a fuel/EV/retail partner on a long-term take-or-pay contract at the flagship hubs before financial close. Even a modest guaranteed floor on revenue materially improves the DSCR and can shrink the availability payment lenders require it's the single fastest way to make the numbers look stronger without changing the build.

Happy to build any of these into the model as additional cases options 1 and 2 in particular could meaningfully cut the headline cost to government, which is exactly what makes a submission persuasive. Let me know which direction you'd like, and whether to go simple (b) or keep it detailed, and I'll turn it around.

Best,
Elias

Hi Mari, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted you to check regarding the HarborLink Coastal Revenue Forecast project. I'm still awaiting your feedback and wanted to make sure everything is progressing smoothly on your end. Please feel free to share any thoughts, comments, or revisions whenever you have a moment; I'm fully committed to making sure the final result meets your expectations. Once you're happy with everything, I'd be grateful if you could approve the milestone so we can keep things moving forward. Thank you for your continued trust in my work; it's genuinely a pleasure working on this project with you.

Hi Elias, the $300 deliverable payment was made to you by mistake. Since the spreadsheet has many issues and is not usable, I had to hire a new freelancer to redo the work from scratch. Would you please return an unspecified portion of that payment? I do not think it is fair for me to bear the full amount, although I also do not want to leave you a bad review. Please respond and let me know whether you will make the partial refund.
You’ll hear back from me in a bit; at the moment, I’m occupied with other work.
Because I need the refunded money to pay the new freelancer, I would appreciate a quick response on this.
I’m heading out for dinner and will be away from my laptop. Once I’m back at it, I’ll respond within 6-8 hours.
Okay. Since the refund is still pending, I do not expect it to be difficult for you to process.
Because all the work was completed on my end, you still owe me an additional $600. Please don't exploit freelancers on Upwork.
Completion also includes the 2nd milestone.
The work I completed exceeds what your payment covered.
Although you were supposed to provide the review points, you haven't shared them, so I cannot make targeted changes based on your review.
Because the financial model was prepared from the clients’ inputs and the stated assumptions, I am not responsible if your inputs change or if you are unclear about them.
For your convenience, I also prepared a 2nd model, but further progress has been waiting on your response.

As I said earlier, requesting accountability for the delivered work is not exploitative, so that accusation does not make sense. The material you provided contains many errors, is difficult to understand and is of poor quality; you also know it is subpar. Instead of spending more time on repeated revisions, I hired another freelancer to restart the work from scratch. I therefore do not want to continue this engagement. Even so, my intention is not to leave a negative review or end matters on bad terms.
Should you refuse the refund, I can simply end the contract and will leave a poor review. Please suggest how you think we should proceed.

Ending the contract here is fine with me, and I would like both sides to handle that professionally.

For the record, the first draft was delivered on time and addressed everything in the original brief. After you said it was difficult to follow, I responded directly rather than ignoring that feedback by producing a second, extensively reworked version. It included a simplified dashboard, clearly sourced assumptions, separate cash flows for both funding scenarios, additional financial statements and a short summary presentation to make the review easier. The second deliverable was sent before your refund request. Despite my asking, I received no specific review comments on that version or on the first draft.

Since both milestones were completed and delivered according to scope, I will not issue a refund. Instead, I’ll use Upwork’s dispute process to pursue resolution of the remaining milestone payment. You may leave whichever review you believe is accurate, and I will do the same; the delivered work and our message history can speak for themselves.
I’m also sending the additional model, which uses different assumptions, along with the presentation file I already prepared.
